Two honest caveats that keep the recommendation mostly intact: (a) these are DOT-registered motor carriers, not repair shops, so it fills shop email only for the subset of repair operations that also hold a DOT number — a join to be measured, not assumed; (b) many are sole-proprietor personal Gmail addresses, so bulk republication is a PII question, not just a licence question. Licence claim also PARTIAL: the dataset self-declares 'unknown-license', not public domain — 17 USC 105 makes PD the sensible default but do not assert it as the publisher's stated terms.

verdict_summary:
All 12 claimed URLs resolve; none is fabricated. The researcher's OSM empirical work is excellent — I reproduced every fill rate to the decimal (272 rows exactly, brand 55.9%, brand:wikidata 39.3%, check_date 4.0%, email 5/272, contact:mobile 0/272, opening_hours 44/272 with exactly 2 = "24/7"). The single most important claim, that Overture Places carries no ODbL share-alike, is correct and I verified it structurally: Places is the only theme on the attribution page missing the "License for theme: ODbL" line every other theme has. The three ToS prohibitions (Love's, TA, Ryder) are confirmed with verbatim quotes.

Four material errors, roughly in order of damage:

1. FMCSA "has no email column" is wrong. The dataset has 147 columns, not 57 — the researcher read the keys of one sampled Socrata row, and Socrata drops nulls per-row. email_address has 2,939,689 non-null values. The blanket "no US government dataset publishes business contact emails in bulk" is false. Caveat that preserves most of his conclusion: these are motor carriers, not repair shops, and many are personal Gmail addresses, so it is a PII question as much as a licence one. His licence line is also loose — the dataset self-declares "unknown-license", not public domain.

2. FSQ OS Places is gated, not keyless (401 on every file), and is not 19 months stale — there are 20 monthly releases through dt=2026-07-09. The staleness objection to date_refreshed collapses. I found the keyless replacement: the public S3 bucket fsq-os-places-us-east-1 serves Apache-2.0 LICENSE.txt and NOTICE.txt anonymously.

3. opening-hours-py is MIT OR Apache-2.0, not AGPL. No copyleft risk; safe to vendor.

4. service:vehicle:welding, :roadside_assistance, :towing, :breakdown and :mobile_mechanic_service all exist on taginfo (729 subkeys, not "40+"). His recommendation still stands, but on different evidence: those tags are absent from the US truck_repair set, not absent from OSM.

One gap: AllThePlaces (CC0 1.0, live loves_us spider, already an Overture Places source) makes Love's/Speedco locations legally obtainable without touching loves.com.
